mcq.q: A late spring frost after budburst is more likely on
choices: A Steep mid-slopes with air drainage
B Low-lying hollows and valley floors where cold air pools
C Windy hilltops that never cool
mcq.answer: B Low-lying hollows and valley floors where cold air pools
mcq.why: Frost flows downhill; heaters, wind machines and aspersion are the defences.

mcq.q: The main reason many quality estates harvest at night or in the cool morning is to
choices: B Bring in cooler fruit, slowing oxidation and microbial activity
D Raise the must temperature to 35 °C
mcq.answer: B Bring in cooler fruit, slowing oxidation and microbial activity
mcq.why: Especially useful for whites and in warm climates.

mcq.q: Sustainable viticulture, as taught at this level, aims to
choices: A Ban all sulphur and copper by law everywhere
B Reduce unnecessary sprays and inputs while remaining commercially viable
mcq.answer: B Reduce unnecessary sprays and inputs while remaining commercially viable
mcq.why: Organic and biodynamic are stricter subsets; ‘sustainable’ is a broader, often certified, middle path.

mcq.q: Shoot thinning and positioning after budburst are forms of
choices: B Canopy management to control yield, shade and disease
mcq.answer: B Canopy management to control yield, shade and disease
mcq.why: Summer work (ébourgeonnage, rognage, leafing) fine-tunes what winter pruning began.

mcq.q: A pied de cuve is
choices: B A small starter ferment used to multiply yeast before inoculation
mcq.answer: B A small starter ferment used to multiply yeast before inoculation
mcq.why: Used for both cultured and ambient yeasts to get a strong start.

mcq.q: Cold stabilisation of a white wine is used to
choices: B Precipitate tartrate crystals so they do not form in the customer’s fridge
mcq.answer: B Precipitate tartrate crystals so they do not form in the customer’s fridge
mcq.why: A cosmetic/stability step; it does not mean the wine is sweet.

mcq.q: Flash détente or similar heat-and-vacuum treatments on red grapes are designed to
choices: B Extract colour and aroma quickly before a shorter ferment
D Replace pressing of whites only
mcq.answer: B Extract colour and aroma quickly before a shorter ferment
mcq.why: Modern extraction kit; more common in warm, high-volume or thick-skinned reds.

mcq.q: Leaving a white wine on full (gross) lees for months without racking risks
choices: A Nothing at all in every case
B Reduction and off-sulphides if the lees are not healthy or stirred/managed
C Automatic improvement equal to new oak
mcq.answer: B Reduction and off-sulphides if the lees are not healthy or stirred/managed
mcq.why: Fine lees can be a texture tool; dirty gross lees can spoil a wine.

mcq.q: Pessac-Léognan dry whites are typically
choices: B Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, often barrel-fermented
mcq.answer: B Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, often barrel-fermented
mcq.why: The serious white pair of northern Graves; oak and lees are common.

mcq.q: Côtes de Bourg and Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux are
choices: B Right-bank-side, often Merlot-led reds at a friendlier price than Pomerol
mcq.answer: B Right-bank-side, often Merlot-led reds at a friendlier price than Pomerol
mcq.why: The Gironde’s other bank, north of Bourg/Blaye; everyday Bordeaux.

mcq.q: Morey-Saint-Denis sits between Gevrey and Chambolle and has
choices: B Several red Grand Crus (for example Clos de Tart, Clos de la Roche)
mcq.answer: B Several red Grand Crus (for example Clos de Tart, Clos de la Roche)
mcq.why: A smaller Côte de Nuits village that is easy to skip in revision — do not.

mcq.q: Santenay and Maranges are
choices: A The southern end of the Côte de Beaune, mainly red Pinot
mcq.answer: A The southern end of the Côte de Beaune, mainly red Pinot
mcq.why: Less famous than Volnay/Pommard; still Côte d’Or Pinot.

mcq.q: Saumur blanc is often
choices: B A dry or sparkling Chenin from tuffeau around Saumur
mcq.answer: B A dry or sparkling Chenin from tuffeau around Saumur
mcq.why: The same town as Saumur-Champigny (red) and much Crémant de Loire.

mcq.q: Coteaux de l’Aubance is
choices: B A sweet (and some dry) Chenin AOC in Anjou, smaller than Layon
mcq.answer: B A sweet (and some dry) Chenin AOC in Anjou, smaller than Layon
mcq.why: Another Loire sweet Chenin valley; do not invent it as a red AOC.

mcq.q: Hermitage blanc is
choices: B Marsanne and Roussanne, full-bodied and long-lived
mcq.answer: B Marsanne and Roussanne, full-bodied and long-lived
mcq.why: One of France’s most age-worthy whites; often some oak.

mcq.q: Cairanne (promoted from villages status) is a
choices: B Southern Rhône named red (and white) AOC, Grenache-based for reds
mcq.answer: B Southern Rhône named red (and white) AOC, Grenache-based for reds
mcq.why: Learn the southern village ladder: generic CdR, Villages, named villages, then CDP/Gigondas etc.

mcq.q: Fitou and Corbières in the Languedoc are
choices: B Warm Mediterranean reds, often Carignan with Grenache and Syrah
mcq.answer: B Warm Mediterranean reds, often Carignan with Grenache and Syrah
mcq.why: Fitou is split geographically; old Carignan on hills is the quality story.

mcq.q: Alsace Grand Cru Zotzenberg is unusual because it may include
choices: B Sylvaner as a permitted Grand Cru variety on that site
mcq.answer: B Sylvaner as a permitted Grand Cru variety on that site
mcq.why: Most Alsace Grand Crus are Riesling, Pinot Gris, Gewurz, Muscat; a few exceptions exist — do not invent extra ones.

mcq.q: Barolo Chinato is
choices: A A dry table Nebbiolo with no ageing
B An aromatised wine based on Barolo; not the standard DOCG table wine
mcq.answer: B An aromatised wine based on Barolo; not the standard DOCG table wine
mcq.why: If it appears, know it is flavoured; the exam still wants you to know Barolo the table wine.

mcq.q: Chianti (not Classico) covers
choices: B A wider Tuscan zone with several sub-zones (Rùfina, Colli Senesi…), still Sangiovese-based
mcq.answer: B A wider Tuscan zone with several sub-zones (Rùfina, Colli Senesi…), still Sangiovese-based
mcq.why: Classico is the historic inner hills and a separate DOCG.

mcq.q: Amarone’s legal alcohol is high because
choices: A The wine is always fortified
B Dried grapes have more sugar, so a dry ferment yields more alcohol
C It is a tank sparkler
mcq.answer: B Dried grapes have more sugar, so a dry ferment yields more alcohol
mcq.why: Typically 14%+; residual sugar would make Recioto, not Amarone.

mcq.q: Verdicchio di Matelica, compared with Castelli di Jesi, is often
choices: B More inland and sometimes a little more structured
mcq.answer: B More inland and sometimes a little more structured
mcq.why: Two Marche homes for the same grape.

mcq.q: Yecla, inland from Jumilla, shares a focus on
choices: B Monastrell in a hot, dry south-east
mcq.answer: B Monastrell in a hot, dry south-east
mcq.why: Murcia’s high plateau; ripe, often inexpensive reds.

mcq.q: Ribeiro in Galicia is known for
choices: B Blended whites (Treixadura and friends), fuller than many Rías Baixas
mcq.answer: B Blended whites (Treixadura and friends), fuller than many Rías Baixas
mcq.why: Inland valleys; a different Galician white conversation.

mcq.q: A Rioja white Gran Reserva, if you see one, has been
choices: B Aged far longer than a joven white; traditional examples are nutty and oaky
C Always a Sauvignon tank wine
mcq.answer: B Aged far longer than a joven white; traditional examples are nutty and oaky
mcq.why: Rare; the legal white/rosé ageing minima are shorter than for red but Gran Reserva still means time.

mcq.q: Burgenland in Austria is a source of
choices: B Blaufränkisch reds and, around the Neusiedlersee, botrytis sweet wines
mcq.answer: B Blaufränkisch reds and, around the Neusiedlersee, botrytis sweet wines
mcq.why: Warmer east; Ruster Ausbruch is the historic sweet wine.

mcq.q: Eszencia in Tokaj is
choices: B The free-run syrup from aszú berries, extremely sweet, barely fermentable
mcq.answer: B The free-run syrup from aszú berries, extremely sweet, barely fermentable
mcq.why: The rarest Tokaj; tiny yields, tiny alcohol.

mcq.q: Távora-Varosa in Portugal is better known for
choices: B Sparkling wine (and some still) in the highlands south of the Douro
mcq.answer: B Sparkling wine (and some still) in the highlands south of the Douro
mcq.why: A reminder that Portugal’s fizz is not only Vinho Verde spritz.

mcq.q: Touriga Nacional as a table-wine grape, outside a Port blend, typically gives
choices: A Pale colour and no aroma
B Deep colour, floral perfume and firm tannin
mcq.answer: B Deep colour, floral perfume and firm tannin
mcq.why: Dão and Douro dry reds often show it more clearly than a multi-variety Port.

mcq.q: Anderson Valley in Mendocino is valued for
choices: A The hottest Zinfandel in the Central Valley
B Cool, foggy Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and aromatic whites, plus sparkling base
mcq.answer: B Cool, foggy Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and aromatic whites, plus sparkling base
mcq.why: A coastal valley that opens to the Pacific; Gewurz is a local extra.

mcq.q: Elqui and Limarí in northern Chile are
choices: A The hottest Central Valley floors only
B Northerly, often high or coastal-influenced valleys for crisp whites and some Syrah
mcq.answer: B Northerly, often high or coastal-influenced valleys for crisp whites and some Syrah
mcq.why: Limarí’s limestone and cloud; Elqui’s altitude and clear skies.

mcq.q: Adelaide Hills is a South Australian GI for
choices: B Cooler-climate Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Pinot and some sparkling
mcq.answer: B Cooler-climate Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Pinot and some sparkling
mcq.why: Altitude above Adelaide; a contrast with Barossa and McLaren Vale.

mcq.q: Hawke’s Bay Syrah, especially from Gimblett Gravels, is typically
choices: B A moderate-climate, peppery, relatively fine Syrah, not a Barossa blockbuster
mcq.answer: B A moderate-climate, peppery, relatively fine Syrah, not a Barossa blockbuster
mcq.why: New Zealand’s most convincing Syrah story.

mcq.q: A French wine labelled AOC/AOP must
choices: A Come from the named area and follow that AOC’s grape and production rules
B Only state a variety, with no place
mcq.answer: A Come from the named area and follow that AOC’s grape and production rules
mcq.why: AOP is the EU PDO name; AOC remains the usual French label word.

mcq.q: Chianti Classico Gran Selezione is
choices: A A PGI with no ageing
B A top ageing/quality tier above Riserva, from estate grapes
mcq.answer: B A top ageing/quality tier above Riserva, from estate grapes
mcq.why: Know Joven/Crianza is Spain; Riserva/Gran Selezione is Chianti Classico.

mcq.q: If a US wine names a state (California) the federal minimum from that state is
mcq.why: State 75%; AVA 85%; Oregon is stricter for many claims.

mcq.q: Reserve wines in non-vintage Champagne are used to
choices: B Blend for consistency, weight and a house signature across vintages
mcq.answer: B Blend for consistency, weight and a house signature across vintages
mcq.why: A library of older vins clairs is a major house asset.

mcq.q: Disgorgement late (recently disgorged) compared with an earlier disgorgement of the same wine usually means
choices: B More youthful autolysis notes kept until closer to sale, then a fresher post-dosage life
C The wine is tank method
D The wine is sweet PX
mcq.answer: B More youthful autolysis notes kept until closer to sale, then a fresher post-dosage life
mcq.why: RD / lately disgorged is a style choice, not a legal sweetness band.

mcq.q: Crémant d’Alsace is typically
choices: B Traditional method from Pinot Blanc, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and related grapes
mcq.answer: B Traditional method from Pinot Blanc, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and related grapes
mcq.why: Alsace’s bottle-fermented wine; still wines of Alsace are a separate story.

mcq.q: Walker Bay and Elgin in South Africa matter to sparkling and still wine because they are
choices: B Cooler coastal or high sites suited to Pinot, Chardonnay and taut still wines
mcq.answer: B Cooler coastal or high sites suited to Pinot, Chardonnay and taut still wines
mcq.why: Cap Classique houses also look to cool fruit; Hemel-en-Aarde is the Pinot address.

mcq.q: A traditional-method rosé gets its colour from
choices: B Short skin contact and/or a little still red wine in the blend (where the law allows)
mcq.answer: B Short skin contact and/or a little still red wine in the blend (where the law allows)
mcq.why: Champagne famously allows the red-wine blend; many others prefer saignée/maceration.

mcq.q: Oloroso that has been sweetened with PX is typically sold as
mcq.answer: B Cream Sherry
mcq.why: Cream is the sweetened oxidative style; Pale Cream is the sweetened biological style.

mcq.q: Garrafeira Port is a rare style that
choices: A Is always a white Port drunk with tonic
B Spends time in wood then a long period in large glass demijohns
mcq.answer: B Spends time in wood then a long period in large glass demijohns
mcq.why: If it appears: wood then glass; most students will meet Vintage, LBV and Tawny first.

mcq.q: Rainwater Madeira is
choices: A A style name, usually a lighter, medium-dry blend, not a weather report
mcq.answer: A A style name, usually a lighter, medium-dry blend, not a weather report
mcq.why: An old market term; do not confuse with harvest rain as a vineyard hazard.

mcq.q: Banyuls Grand Cru (where the mention is used) implies
choices: B Longer oxidative ageing of a Grenache VDN than basic Banyuls
mcq.answer: B Longer oxidative ageing of a Grenache VDN than basic Banyuls
mcq.why: Roussillon’s top traditional sweet red; Maury has a parallel quality story.

mcq.q: Australian vintage fortified Shiraz (the old ‘port’ style) is
choices: B A fortified red made in a Port-like way, now labelled without the word Port for export
mcq.answer: B A fortified red made in a Port-like way, now labelled without the word Port for export
mcq.why: Barossa and others; the EU protects the name Port.

mcq.q: Length of finish on the SAT is how long
choices: A The cork was in the bottle
B Flavour persists after the wine is spat or swallowed
mcq.answer: B Flavour persists after the wine is spat or swallowed
mcq.why: Short / medium(−) / medium / medium(+) / long — not a quality word by itself, but short often limits quality.

mcq.q: A screwcap wine stored upright in a hot car for a week will likely
choices: B Taste cooked or oxidised because heat, not oxygen through cork, was the problem
mcq.answer: B Taste cooked or oxidised because heat, not oxygen through cork, was the problem
mcq.why: Closure does not save a wine from heat.

mcq.q: A very oaky, high-alcohol white with a delicate steamed fish will typically
choices: B Overwhelm the dish; a leaner, higher-acid white would be kinder
C Soften tannin that is not there in the fish
mcq.answer: B Overwhelm the dish; a leaner, higher-acid white would be kinder
mcq.why: Match weight and intensity; oak and heat bully gentle food.

mcq.q: Complexity on the SAT refers to
choices: B A range of flavours from fruit, process and/or age, not a single note
C The number of bottles produced
mcq.answer: B A range of flavours from fruit, process and/or age, not a single note
mcq.why: A simple but clean wine can still be ‘good’; outstanding wines are complex and long.

parts.prompt: Describe the Danube regions (Wachau, Kremstal, Kamptal) in climate, grapes and the Wachau categories.
points: Cool-moderate continental, river influence, terraces, gneiss/loess.
Grüner Veltliner and Riesling are the quality pair.
Wachau: Steinfeder (lightest), Federspiel, Smaragd (ripest, often dry, can age).
Kamptal/Kremstal DAC: typically dry GV and Riesling from defined areas.
Botrytis is less the story here than in Burgenland.
Name a site (Heiligenstein, Achleiten) only if sure.

parts.prompt: How is Tokaji Aszú made, and which grapes are used?
points: Furmint (acid, structure), Hárslevelű (perfume), Sárgamuskotály (Muscat) and others.
Noble rot in humid autumns by the rivers; aszú berries selected.
Macerate aszú in must or base wine; press; slow ferment; oxidative or protective ageing depending on house.
Sweetness historically in puttonyos; modern law simplified (Aszú is always sweet and concentrated).
Eszencia and Szamorodni as related wines.
Not a fortified wine in the Port sense.

parts.prompt: Contrast winery practice for a dry Wachau Smaragd Riesling and a Tokaji Aszú.
points: Smaragd: healthy fruit, ferment dry (steel and/or large old wood), no new-barrique spice, lees, high acid, bottled for age.
Aszú: selected rot, residual sugar, slow ferment, years in cask often, oxidative notes possible, luscious but acid-framed.
Both can age for decades if balanced.
Do not chaptalise a Prädikat-like sweet Tokaj as if it lacked sugar.
Service: Smaragd lightly chilled; Aszú cooler, small glass, sweet food or blue cheese.

parts.prompt: Outline the climate of the Western Cape and the roles of the Benguela current, mountains and wind.
points: Mediterranean: wet winter, dry summer.
Benguela current cools the coast; fog and breeze.
Mountains create cooler aspects and rain shadows; many quality wards are coastal or high.
Cape Doctor wind dries and can damage but reduces disease.
Inland (some BreedeKloof/Robertson sites) can be much hotter.
Irrigation is common in dry wards.

parts.prompt: For Chenin Blanc, Pinotage and Cabernet/Bordeaux blends, name a typical district or ward and a style.
points: Chenin: most planted; Stellenbosch, Swartland, Citrusdal — from fresh tank to old-vine, oak, skin-contact.
Pinotage: Pinot × Cinsaut; can be carbonic and fruity or serious and structured (Stellenbosch, Wellington); burnt rubber is a fault not a goal.
Cabernet and blends: Stellenbosch (especially warmer parts, Helderberg/Simonsberg), structured, often oak.
Swartland: old bush vines, Rhône varieties, Chenin, whole cluster, less new oak — a modern quality story.
Constantia: historic sweet and now Sauvignon/Chardonnay in a cool south peninsula.
Walker Bay: Pinot and Chardonnay.

parts.prompt: What does Wine of Origin guarantee, and how might a Swartland Chenin be made for texture rather than primary fruit?
points: WO: 100% from the stated area (estate/ward/district/region); variety and vintage claims have high minima.
Texture Chenin: older vines, later pick or skin contact, old oak or concrete, lees, maybe oxidative handling, MLF optional, less new toast.
Contrast with a cool tank, early-pick supermarket Chenin.
Neither is fortified.
State a quality risk: oxidation or phenolics if handling is clumsy.

parts.prompt: Compare Champagne with Crémant de Loire and Crémant de Bourgogne in grapes, climate and typical style.
points: Champagne: PN, Meunier, Chardonnay; cool chalk; long lees for NV/vintage; high acid, autolysis, global brand blending.
Crémant de Loire: Chenin, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, etc.; maritime-moderate; apple/quince from Chenin; traditional method, shorter legal lees than vintage Champagne.
Crémant de Bourgogne: Chardonnay and Pinot (plus Aligoté etc.); regional fruit including Chablis/Chalonnaise/Mâconnais; closer flavour to Champagne when from cool sites.
All are traditional method; none may use the word Champagne.
Price and lees time are the usual quality gap, not the method.
Award for Crémant d’Alsace or Limoux as extra accurate contrast.

parts.prompt: Which legal or practical rules keep Crémant from simply being ‘cheap Champagne’?
points: Different regions, grapes and AOCs — you cannot blend in Champagne fruit and call it Crémant or vice versa.
Yield, press fractions and minimum lees are defined per AOC.
Climate gives a different acid/fruit balance.
Houses do not have the same reserve-wine libraries or brands.
Some Crémants are excellent; the category is not a quality insult.
Hand harvest is required for Crémant in France.

parts.prompt: Suggest service and a food use for a Brut Crémant de Loire made from Chenin.
points: Well chilled; aperitif or with goat’s cheese (Loire classic) or apple tart if a little dosage.
Chenin’s acid and apple/quince sit with chèvre better than a very toasty prestige Champagne.
Drink on release; a few top cuvées age.
White-wine glass is fine.
Avoid a dish sweeter than the wine or a very tannic steak.

parts.prompt: Explain where tannin in a red wine comes from and how ripeness and winemaking change its feel.
points: Skins, seeds and stems; oak adds its own tannin.
Unripe seeds/stems: green, bitter, astringent.
Ripe skins: riper, riper-feeling tannin; longer maceration extracts more.
Oak and time polymerise tannin so it feels finer.
Variety: Nebbiolo, Cabernet, Tannat, Aglianico are high; Gamay, Pinot, Grenache lower.
Press wine is tougher than free-run.

parts.prompt: How should you serve a young Barolo or Cabernet that is high in tannin, and what food helps?
points: About 16–18 °C, not 22 °C; a large glass; decant for air (and later for sediment).
Protein and fat (roast beef, hard cheese) bind tannin.
Avoid chilli, very sweet glazes and delicate poached fish.
Umami without fat (soy, tomato) can make tannin harsher — add oil or cheese.
A decade in bottle may do more than 10 minutes in a decanter, but both can help.
Do not serve ice-cold (tannin shouts).

parts.prompt: Contrast that advice with service of a high-tannin dry Oloroso or a young Vintage Port.
points: Oloroso: not high in grape-skin tannin in the same way; serve lightly cool, nutty/savoury food, lasts after opening.
Vintage Port: tannin plus residual sugar plus alcohol — decant, slightly cool, blue cheese or chocolate; sweetness changes the tannin feel.
Do not treat Oloroso like Fino (fragile, very cold).
Do not treat young Vintage Port like a 20-year tawny (no crust, more nutty, more stable open).
Alcohol in Port clashes with chilli just as in a dry red.
Storage: Port vintage on its side; opened tawny/Oloroso are more tolerant.
